newsitem.title: FRANCE: More political prisoners jailed in Syria - report.
newsitem.headline: More political prisoners jailed in Syria - report.

text.p: The number of political prisoners in Syrian jails rose to 2,800 in 1996, about a hundred more than the previous year, a Syrian human rights group reported on Tuesday.

The increase was the first since 1989 in the number of political prisoners in Syria, which had been steadily falling for the previous six years, said the Committee for the Defence of Democratic Freedoms and Human Rights in its annual report for 1996.
The increase was due to the arrest of more than 100 individuals during the year due to their political beliefs while just five were released, said the Paris-based group.
Those being held included Lebanese and Palestinians as well as Syrians, it said.
Under martial law in effect since 1963, Syrian citizens "do not have the right to form associations, organisations or political parties in order to express or defend their opinions," the group said.
"Workers and student groups are infiltrated, particularly with regard to their activities and their elections. Their directors are often imposed on them," it said.
